subject.title: Hard-delete or runtimeId migration needed for @apify/apify-openclaw-plugin

question: Should an authorized ClawHub admin apply the audited runtimeId repair for `@apify/apify-openclaw-plugin` from `apify` to `apify-openclaw-plugin`, or choose a hard-delete/decline path after authority and collision checks?
rationale: This changes executable plugin identity and package reservation state in production, so source automation cannot safely make the security-boundary decision or verify publisher authority.

options.title: Run guarded runtimeId repair
options.body: Use the admin dry-run/apply flow after verifying Apify authority, current package state, and no active runtimeId collision.

options.title: Hard-delete or retire entry
options.body: Use a destructive package repair path only if the runtimeId repair cannot preserve the intended package identity safely.

options.title: Hold pending stronger proof
options.body: Keep the issue blocked until maintainers receive enough publisher or organizational proof to authorize the production mutation.

recommendation.title: Run guarded runtimeId repair
recommendation.body: Use the admin dry-run/apply flow after verifying Apify authority, current package state, and no active runtimeId collision.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the merged admin package repair flows and handled the analogous OpenViking repair path.
